items.title: Section: The Remaining Five Reflections — Firm, Bright, Sincere, Joyful, Great — Closing the First Aspect

items.zh: 六者、作意思惟：我於如是堅固對治，不為一切漏有漏法、一切魔軍之所勝伏；七者、作意思惟：我今能於一切佛法，其心無有怯劣而轉；八者、作意思惟：我今能於一切苦行，無有怯弱；九者、作意思惟：我心一向於大乘中深生信解，終不愛樂餘下劣乘；十者、作意思惟：我於一切利有情事，深心愛樂。由此十種淨心意樂作意思惟，能入菩薩增上心住。
items.en:
Sixth, reflecting: within this firm remedy, one is not overcome by any contaminated, defiling dharma, nor by any army of demonic forces. Seventh, reflecting: towards every buddha-dharma, the mind now turns without timidity or inferiority. Eighth, reflecting: towards every ascetic hardship, there is now no timidity at all. Ninth, reflecting: the mind is single-mindedly, deeply resolved towards and understanding of the great vehicle, never delighting in any lesser, inferior vehicle. Tenth, reflecting: towards every undertaking benefiting sentient beings, one delights in this profoundly and deeply.
Fourth, the conclusion. By these ten kinds of purified-mind aspiration and reflection, one is able to enter the bodhisattva's abode of heightened mind.
Commentary: Regarding "further, by ten other kinds of purified-mind aspiration" and the like — the Ten Grounds Sutra says: a bodhisattva, having genuinely purified the mind and practised the second ground, wishing to attain the third bodhisattva ground, should give rise to ten kinds of deep, mindful reflection. What are the ten? First, pure mind. Second, unmoving mind. Third, aversion-mind. Fourth, desire-freed mind. Fifth, non-regressing mind. Sixth, firm mind. Seventh, bright and flourishing mind. Eighth, sincere and generous mind. Ninth, joyful mind. Tenth, great mind. A bodhisattva, by these ten kinds of deep, mindful reflection, attains entry into the third ground, each explained individually in the Commentary on the Ten Grounds Sutra. The ten kinds of purified-mind aspiration spoken of here should be understood to correspond in this order.

items.title: Section: Deep Aversion Towards All Conditioned Formations, and Deep Longing for the Buddhas' Own Wisdom

items.zh: 菩薩安住增上心住，能以種種過患行相壞一切行，於彼諸行深心厭離。於佛妙智，能以種種勝利行相，見大勝利。又於其中，能以淳淨一味欲樂，深生愛慕。
items.en:
Second aspect: thoroughly penetrating formations, the buddhas' own wisdom, and the realm of sentient beings; first, genuine penetration; first, regarding formations. Bodhisattvas abiding in the abode of heightened mind, through every kind of aspect displaying faults and calamities, are able to break down every formation entirely, giving rise to deeply felt aversion towards them.
Commentary: Regarding "every kind of aspect displaying faults and calamities" — the Ten Grounds Sutra says: correctly observe that conditioned dharmas, every formation, are impermanent, suffering, impure, impermanent and decaying, not abiding long, arising and perishing moment by moment, coming from no prior boundary, going to no later boundary, not abiding even in the present. One should correctly observe every formation in just this way, exactly as explained there.
Second, regarding the buddhas' own wisdom. Towards the buddhas' own wondrous wisdom, through every kind of aspect displaying excellent benefit, one beholds its great excellence. Furthermore, within this, with a single, purely undivided savour of longing, one deeply gives rise to love and admiration.
Commentary: Regarding "every kind of aspect displaying excellent benefit" — the Ten Grounds Sutra says: this bodhisattva sees the Tathāgata's own wisdom as inconceivable, peerless, immeasurable, rare, unmixed, untroubled, unafflicted with grief, able to reach the great, fearless city of peace, never to turn back again, and sees it able to rescue immeasurable, suffering sentient beings. This should be explained exactly as there.

items.title: Section: Ten Kinds of Superior Mind Towards Suffering Sentient Beings — Pitiable, Impoverished, Imprisoned, Overgrown, Lost

items.zh: 於有情界，能以種種苦惱行相，觀為有苦；於諸有情興悲戀心，生依義心。
items.en:
Third, regarding sentient beings. Towards the realm of sentient beings, through every kind of aspect displaying suffering and hardship, one observes that they have suffering; towards sentient beings, one arouses a heart of grief and compassion, giving rise to a mind of loving-kindness intent on their welfare.
Commentary: Regarding "every kind of aspect displaying suffering and hardship" — the Ten Grounds Sutra says: seeing that every conditioned formation holds immeasurable suffering and hardship, one further gives rise, towards all sentient beings, to ten kinds of superior mind. Namely: sentient beings are pitiable, solitary, without rescue — giving rise to superior mind; they are perpetually impoverished — giving rise to superior mind; the fire of the three poisons blazes unceasing — giving rise to superior mind; they are shut within the firm prison of the three realms of existence — giving rise to superior mind; they are perpetually covered by the dense thicket of affliction and evil — giving rise to superior mind; they lack the power of correct observation — giving rise to superior mind; departed from wholesome dharma, the mind knows no joy — giving rise to superior mind; they have lost the buddhas' own wondrous teaching — giving rise to superior mind; they perpetually follow the world's own current — giving rise to superior mind; they have lost the very means to nirvana — giving rise to superior mind. These are called the ten kinds of superior mind. This should be explained exactly as there.

items.title: Section: Three Resulting Actions — No Laxity, Blazing Diligence, Vast Compassion — Closing the Second Aspect

items.zh: 於一切行無有放逸，為大菩提熾然精進，於諸有情能起廣大悲愍意樂。
items.en:
Second, clarifying the resulting action. Towards every formation, there is no laxity. For the sake of great awakening, diligence blazes forth. Towards every sentient being, one is able to arouse a vast heart of compassionate grief.
Commentary: Regarding "towards every formation, there is no laxity" and the like — this displays that, genuine penetration now accomplished, one is able to correctly act. Because of deep aversion and freedom from desire towards formations, there is no laxity towards them. Because of beholding the buddha-wisdom's own excellence and deeply longing for it, diligence blazes forth for its sake. Because of observing that sentient beings suffer, one is thereby able to arouse a vast heart of compassionate grief towards them.

items.title: Section: Seeking the Ultimate Means of Liberation — Non-Discriminating Wisdom, Resting on Supreme Absorption, Resting on Hearing the True Dharma

items.zh: 觀諸有情解脫眾苦究竟方便，唯是一切煩惱諸纏無障礙智；觀彼解脫能圓證者，唯於法界一切分別現行雜染生起對治無分別慧；觀能成辦彼智光明，唯是無倒勝三摩地；觀所引發一切靜慮、等持、等至，皆菩薩藏聽聞為先，皆聞正法以為緣起。
items.en: Third aspect: seeking out the means for sentient beings' liberation from suffering. Observing that the ultimate means for sentient beings' liberation from every suffering is nothing other than an unobstructed wisdom regarding every entanglement of affliction; observing that what allows this liberation to be fully realised is nothing other than a non-discriminating wisdom that gives rise to the remedy for every defiling discrimination currently manifesting within the dharma-realm; observing that what accomplishes this wisdom's own illumination is nothing other than an undistorted, excellent state of absorption; observing that every meditative state, concentration, and attainment thus brought forth is, without exception, preceded by hearing what is proclaimed in the bodhisattva canon, arising altogether through hearing the true dharma as its condition.

items.title: Section: Reverence for the True Dharma — Willing to Leap Into a Blazing Pit for a Single Verse

items.zh: 觀見是已，發大精進訪求多聞。為聞正法，不惜身命，無有資財內外愛物而不能捨，無有師長不誓承事，無有尊教不誓奉行，無有身苦而不誓受。若聞佛法一四句頌，歡喜勇躍，勝得三千大千世界充滿其中大珍寶聚。聞一句法是佛所說，能引正等覺，能淨菩薩行，歡喜踊躍，勝得一切釋、梵、護世轉輪王等極尊貴位。設有告言：善男子聽！我有一句佛所說法，能引正等覺，能淨菩薩行，汝欲聞不？汝今若能投大火坑受大苦者，當為汝說。菩薩聞已，歡喜踊躍，答言：我能！我若得聞如前所說一句法義，正使火坑量等三千大千世界滿中熾火，我從梵天尚投身入，況小火坑。為求佛法，尚應久處大那落迦受大苦惱，況餘小苦而不應受。
items.en:
Fourth aspect: reverence for the true dharma, seeking it tirelessly; first, arousing great diligence. Having observed this, one arouses great diligence, seeking out extensive learning. For the sake of hearing the true dharma, not begrudging life itself; no wealth, no object of attachment inner or outer, that cannot be relinquished; no teacher one would not vow to serve; no instruction one would not vow to uphold; no bodily suffering one would not vow to endure.
Second, joyful exuberance. Upon hearing even a single four-line verse of buddha-dharma, one's joyful exuberance surpasses receiving a great trichiliocosm entirely filled with a great mass of treasure. Hearing a single verse spoken by a buddha, able to draw forth correct, complete awakening, able to purify bodhisattva conduct, one's joyful exuberance surpasses attaining every exalted rank of Śakra, Brahmā, a world-protector, or a universal monarch.
Third, enduring great suffering; first, the hypothetical declaration. Suppose someone declares: good son, listen! I have a single verse of buddha-dharma, able to draw forth correct, complete awakening, able to purify bodhisattva conduct — do you wish to hear it? If you are now able to leap into a great pit of fire and endure great suffering, I shall then teach it to you.
Second, the fitting reply. The bodhisattva, having heard this, joyfully exuberant, replies: I am able! If I may hear the meaning of the verse spoken of before, even were the fire-pit's size equal to an entire great trichiliocosm filled with blazing fire, I would leap in bodily from the Brahma heaven itself — how much more so a small pit of fire. For the sake of seeking buddha-dharma, I should be willing to dwell long in the great hell itself, enduring great suffering — how much more so should I not endure any lesser suffering.

items.title: Section: True Practice Means Actually Practising — Not Just Hearing Words and Sounds — Cultivating Mundane Absorption to Tame Beings' Pride

items.zh: 菩薩發起如是精進，求正法已；復能如實如理思惟，要正修行法隨法行，方得名為隨順佛法，非但聽聞文字、音聲而得清淨。如是知已，即依所聞正緣法相，遠離諸欲惡不善法，廣說乃至能得世俗四種靜慮、四無色定，及四無量、五種神通具足安住。
items.en:
Fifth aspect: correctly practising and attaining abiding stability; first, genuine reflection. A bodhisattva, having aroused such diligence and sought the true dharma, is further able to reflect genuinely and rationally: correct practice means practising dharma in accordance with dharma; only this is called according with buddha-dharma — not merely hearing its words and sounds and thereby attaining purity.
Second, cultivating in reliance on what was heard. Knowing this, relying on what has been heard, correctly attending to the characteristics of phenomena, departing from sensory desires and unwholesome dharmas — in stages explained at length — one is able to attain the four mundane meditative absorptions, the four formless attainments, the four immeasurables, and the five spiritual powers, dwelling fully equipped in all of them.

items.title: Section: Rebirth According to Vow — Relinquishing the Higher Realms, Severing the Fetters of Desire, Existence, and View

items.zh: 既多住已，復還棄捨諸靜慮等、等持、等至，願自在力還來欲界。觀彼彼處，若為有情能作義利，若能圓滿菩提分法，即便往生。非但自在而生彼處。如是菩薩離欲貪故，名斷欲縛；棄捨靜慮、等持、等至故，名斷有縛。菩薩先從勝解行地，於法真如修勝解故，已斷見縛，邪貪恚癡畢竟不轉。
items.en:
Sixth aspect: rebirth according to vow; first, observing genuine benefit. Having long abided in this way, one further relinquishes these meditative absorptions, concentrations, and attainments, and, through the sovereign power of vow, returns to the desire realm. Observing, in this place or that, wherever genuine benefit for sentient beings can be accomplished, or wherever the factors of awakening can be brought to fulfilment, one takes rebirth precisely there — not merely exercising sovereign power while being reborn in such places.
Second, clarifying the severed fetters. Such a bodhisattva, having departed from craving for sensory desire, is said to have severed the fetter of desire. Having relinquished absorption, concentration, and attainment, is said to have severed the fetter of existence. Such a bodhisattva, previously at the stage of resolute practice, having cultivated resolute understanding regarding the suchness of dharmas, has already severed the fetter of view — wrongful craving, hatred, and delusion never again manifesting at all.
Commentary: Regarding "such a bodhisattva, having departed from craving for sensory desire" through "never again manifesting at all" — this explains the earlier cause and condition of the sovereign power of vow, one should understand.

items.title: Section: Purified Wholesome Roots — Gold Entirely Free of Impurity, Weighed and Found Exactly Equal

items.zh: 廣見諸佛、善根清淨，如前應知。此差別者，謂如世間善巧工匠，先所燒鍊手中真金垢穢斯盡，稱量等住。如是菩薩善根清淨，當知亦爾。
items.en:
Seventh aspect: purified wholesome roots; first, pointing to what was already said. Broadly beholding the buddhas, wholesome roots purified, exactly as already explained.
Second, a simile marking the difference. The difference is this: just as, in the world, a skilful craftsman's own already-smelted, genuine gold, held in hand, has every impurity entirely exhausted, weighed and found to abide exactly equal — so too should a bodhisattva's own purified wholesome roots be understood, just so.

items.title: Section: Rebirth as Śakra, Lord of the Thirty-Three Heavens, and Majestic Power a Hundredfold Greater Still

items.zh: 受生多分作釋天帝，善化有情，令離欲貪。所有威力，於前住中已說千數，當知此中有百千數。
items.en:
Eighth, rebirth. Taking rebirth, one most often becomes Śakra, lord of the thirty-three heavens, skilfully transforming sentient beings, causing them to depart from craving and desire.
Ninth, majestic power. Whatever majestic power was already described in the previous abode as a thousand of each kind, one should understand that here it reaches a hundred thousand of each kind.

blocks.text: The third ground is the ground of meditation. Its famous image: a bodhisattva willing to leap into a blazing pit for a single verse of Dharma.

Venerable Miào Jìng: "contamination" is affliction; contaminated dharmas are our eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind. Master Cháng Bǎi: though born in the desire realm, their absorption does not vanish; they give up higher heavens to be born here.

subs.head: Seeing the faults of the conditioned

blocks.text: Venerable Miào Jìng: observing these faults destroys one's own clinging. Master Cháng Bǎi: the world forms and decays, people are born and die.
Venerable Miào Jìng: "a mind reliant on benefit" is loving-kindness, which gives happiness.

"The ultimate means of beings' liberation is nothing but unobstructed wisdom regarding every entanglement of affliction." Venerable Miào Jìng: giving bread relieves hunger only for a while. Wisdom needs samādhi's support; if we only study without meditating, suffering cannot be escaped. Master Cháng Bǎi: reciting the Buddha one moment and thinking of tofu the next is not equipoise.

"Even were the fire pit as large as a great trichiliocosm, I would leap in from the Brahmā heaven, let alone a small pit." Master Cháng Bǎi: in a past life Śākyamuni was willing to gouge out his eyes for one line of Dharma.
Master Cháng Bǎi: one does not think that merely hearing purifies; one must realise it inwardly. Venerable Miào Jìng: understanding first, then practice.
Free of sensual craving, the bond of desire is cut; relinquishing the absorptions, the bond of existence is cut. Venerable Miào Jìng: not bound by desire but bound by absorption is still bondage.
Venerable Miào Jìng: twenty catties, then nineteen, eighteen; once the dross is gone, further burning no longer reduces it.
"Most often reborn as Śakra, transforming beings away from craving."
Master Cháng Bǎi's tofu will make you smile, but it is a fair test. Notice how often the mind slides away during even a few minutes of practice.

quiz.q: In "my mind does not enter contaminated and contaminating dharmas," how does Venerable Miào Jìng explain the terms?
options: "contamination" is affliction; contaminated dharmas are the six faculties; resting in ultimate emptiness, one turns away from them
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "contamination" is affliction; contaminated dharmas are our eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind; resting in the ultimate truth of complete emptiness, one turns away from them.

quiz.q: The third-ground bodhisattva leaves the form realm to be born in the desire realm. Does absorption vanish, according to Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: though born in the desire realm, absorption doesn't vanish — able to go to higher heavens, they choose the desire realm
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: though born in the desire realm, their absorption doesn't vanish; they could go to the form and formless heavens but relinquish them to be born in the desire realm.

quiz.q: "Breaking down every formation through aspects of fault." How do the lectures explain this?
options: Miào Jìng: observing faults breaks one's own clinging; Cháng Bǎi: the world forms and decays, people age and die — and the body is a "moving toilet"
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: observing their faults destroys one's own inner clinging. Master Cháng Bǎi: the world has formation and decay, people birth and death — "breaking down formations"; the body is full of phlegm and filth, a moving toilet.

quiz.q: "Arousing grief and compassion, a mind reliant on benefit (依義心)." How does Venerable Miào Jìng explain it?
options: it is loving-kindness — kindness gives happiness
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "a mind reliant on benefit" is loving-kindness — kindness gives happiness. The English doesn't name it as kindness.

quiz.q: What does the bodhisattva see as the ultimate means of beings' liberation?
options: unobstructed wisdom regarding every entanglement of affliction
quiz.why: "The ultimate means of beings' liberation is nothing but unobstructed wisdom regarding every entanglement of affliction." Master Cháng Bǎi: only wisdom cuts afflictions. Venerable Miào Jìng: giving bread relieves hunger only temporarily.

quiz.q: "What accomplishes this wisdom's light is undistorted samādhi." What does Venerable Miào Jìng stress?
options: wisdom needs samādhi's support to cut afflictions; studying without meditating won't free you
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: wisdom needs samādhi's support; only then has its light the power to cut afflictions; if we just study without meditating, suffering can't be escaped. Master Cháng Bǎi: reciting the Buddha one moment and thinking of tofu the next isn't equipoise.

quiz.q: If told "leap into a great fire pit and I'll tell you one line of dharma," how does the bodhisattva answer?
options: "I can! Even if the pit were the size of a trichiliocosm, I'd leap in from the Brahmā heaven — let alone a small pit"
quiz.why: "I can! Even were the fire pit as large as a great trichiliocosm, I would leap in from the Brahmā heaven — let alone a small pit." Master Cháng Bǎi: in a past life Śākyamuni was willing to gouge out his eyes for one line of dharma.

quiz.q: "Only practising dharma in accordance with dharma accords with the Buddha's teaching — not merely hearing words and sounds." What do the lectures say?
options: Cháng Bǎi: hearing alone doesn't purify — one must realise it inwardly; Miào Jìng: understanding must be followed by practice
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: one doesn't think merely hearing purifies — one must realise it inwardly. Venerable Miào Jìng: there must be understanding and then practice for it to accord with the dharma.

quiz.q: Which three bonds does the bodhisattva sever, and how?
options: freedom from craving cuts the desire bond; relinquishing absorptions the existence bond; the view bond was cut earlier by conviction
quiz.why: Free of sensual craving — the desire bond cut; relinquishing absorptions — the existence bond cut; the view bond was already cut through conviction cultivated at the stage of resolute practice. Venerable Miào Jìng: not bound by desire but bound by absorption is still bondage.

quiz.q: "Pure gold with all impurity exhausted, weighed and found equal." How do the lectures explain "weighed equal"?
options: both: impurities gone, pure gold remains — further smelting no longer reduces it; Miào Jìng: twenty catties burned down until the dross is gone, then it stays
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: after smelting, pure gold doesn't decrease — its weight is constant; all dross removed, it is pure gold. Venerable Miào Jìng: twenty catties, then nineteen, eighteen — once the dross is gone, further burning no longer reduces it.

quiz.q: What does the third-ground bodhisattva often become, and how much greater is the power?
options: Śakra, leading beings from craving; power in the hundred thousands — a hundred times the second ground
quiz.why: "Most often reborn as Śakra, transforming beings away from craving; power, a thousand before, is now a hundred thousand." Master Cháng Bǎi: a hundredfold increase over the second ground.
